title: a list where the schema wants a mapping
notes: The object arm of `analyze_errors`, `not isinstance(data, dict)` branch, now `not_a_mapping_message`. `defs:` renders as an object whose `additionalProperties` is a `BlockType`, and the reproducer writes it as a list of one-key mappings -- the shape a user reaches for when they read `defs:` as "a list of definitions". Three things moved from `[{'greeting': 'hi'}] should be an object`. (1) The value was `str(data)` on a structure, so the user was shown a Python `repr` of the parsed YAML, with Python's quoting and Python's brackets, and not the three words they wrote; `yaml_value` renders it as the YAML it is, behind the same `_VALUE_MAX` wall the `parser:` series uses, and that is what takes Hygiene from 1 to 3. (2) `object` was JSON Schema's noun, taken straight from the schema's `type`, and a reader looking for it in the PDL documentation would not have found it; `mapping` is the word that documentation and the rest of `pdl_diagnostics` already use. (3) There was no suggestion, and `fold_entries` builds one out of the user's own entries rather than inventing an example -- it merges the list of single-entry mappings into the one mapping they were meant to be, refuses when an item is not a mapping or a key is written twice, and `satisfies` checks the result against the same schema before it is offered. `defs: {greeting: hi}` executes and exits 0. Location 1 to 2: the header used to name the line of the `defs` key while the offending list began on the next one. `_walk` records a mapping entry at its key deliberately and the value's own node is not recorded, so `value_location` asks the registry for the value's **first child**, which in block style is on the line the value starts on, and moves the header and the caret there while leaving the path alone -- `  in defs`, not `defs.greeting`, because the claim is about `defs:`. It is 2 and not 3 for the reason every entry in this group is: no `:col`, held at INVENTORY 7.9/7.11 for a separate decision.
